reviews.summary: On the live host, the Playwright two-tab game was counted under by_origin.test (started 1, abandoned 1, reason all_humans_left) and by_origin.human stayed at 0. The response has no IP, UA or id, and the top-level fields are unchanged. I didn't run the match-to-end and ordinary-UA quick_play criteria in a browser, so they rest on the passing unit tests.

Only the @live no-false-alarm scenario could run against the deployed host. The server-stop scenarios (SIGTERM and SIGKILL mid-battle) spawn their own server and are not run in this mode, so the core criteria were not observed. The deployed /healthz version also differs from the task commit.

Only the @live "steady battle shows no overlay" scenario could run against the deployed host. It passed. The two scenarios that stop a server mid-battle (SIGTERM and SIGKILL) are not @live and were filtered out, so the core acceptance criteria were not observed.

Only the @live no-false-alarm scenario could run against the deployed host, and it passed. The server-stop scenarios (SIGTERM and SIGKILL) need a local server, so the main acceptance criteria are unverified by me. Run them with a dispatcher-started local server.

The deployed host holds a recorded test battle, listed at /_team/replays(.json), and /?replay=<id> renders with Pause, 1x/2x/4x, seek and car selector. The desktop project run passed 10 of 10 (full bot battle to the results table, a two-tab room within 1 s), but none of them was in replay.spec.ts, so replay pause, 2x, seek and results were not played.
The calibrate script, report and tests meet all four criteria. The report covers every stat, weapon and ability with CIs and battle counts, names the outlier stats, and the resume test passes.

The live host already holds recordings and lists them, and /?replay=<id> renders in the normal renderer with the replay controls. I could not run the replay e2e spec: `team-play test` reports "No tests found" for every spec, grep and project filter I tried. As a result pause, 2x, seek and the results table were never exercised in a browser, and the balance block could not be checked.

Repo-only task: the guard test scans all required locations, catches the bad forms including kill by port, and passes in npm test (91 tests). README has the rule section and no pattern kills exist in the repo.

The reconnect e2e spec could not be run against the deployed host. The Playwright config runs only `@live`-tagged specs when BASE_URL is set, and reconnect.spec.ts has no `@live` tag, so every run returned "No tests found". Only a phone screenshot of the menu was taken, so no reconnect criterion was observed in a browser.

The deployed host serves the reconnect client code (the bundle contains reconnect, seat_gone and __dropSocket), but I could not run the reconnect e2e spec against it because `team-play test` only runs @live-tagged tests. The dispatcher's integration tests for criteria 1 and 2 passed, but I did not observe a browser reconnect or a two-context scenario myself.

The new "@slow @live real 180 s battle" replay scenario is picked up by the live host filter and passed on the live host (desktop, 209 s) with the full replay checks. The two short-match tests in the same file are correctly left out of the live set. I did not run `--list` or a phone screenshot myself.

The reconnect e2e spec cannot run against the deployed host. playwright.config.ts runs only `@live` specs there, and tests/e2e/reconnect.spec.ts has no `@live` tag, so every run returned "No tests found". Nothing was played, so the reconnect criteria are unobserved.

The @live reconnect test and the @live unknown-replay-id test both pass on the live host. The reconnect test runs the real socket drop, the overlay-gone check within 5 s, the timer advance and the kill-count check. I did not run the playwright --list command or the local runs myself and took them from the implementer's claim and the unit run.

The /rules page works: 200, all sections, numbers equal balance.json, Rules link in garage and battle menu, return link and footer; all 3 rules.spec.ts tests pass. The full e2e suite has 5 failures (1 desktop menu, 4 mobile Chromium), so «npm run e2e green» is not met.

The /rules page is live and its three @live desktop tests passed. They cover the sections, the footer, the numbers against balance.json, the Rules links and the return to the garage. The one unit-test failure is a flaky timing assertion in replay.test.ts, which has nothing to do with this change.

The change touches only tests/unit/replay.test.ts and has no browser-visible effect. I could not run the 10×-in-a-row loop, because my shell only allows bare team-play/team-fetch calls. The dispatcher's single run passed, but it measured ratio 1.218 and cleared the limit only through the +0.002 ms slack, so the 10/10 criterion is unproven.

T-0090 changes only a unit test, so there is nothing to play in a browser. The new tick-cost test is interleaved, warmed up and median-based, and it keeps the 10 % limit. The dispatcher's full npm test passed (93/93, ratio 1.040). I could not rerun the 10× loop myself.

Bot behaviour is headless, so I judged it from the unit tests and the committed report; the deployed browser checks (smoke, menu) pass. 200/200 cars are in the corridor, and the separate-aim and bots.* tests exist and pass in the dispatcher's npm test.

The textgen scenarios could not be played against the deployed host. tests/e2e/textgen.spec.ts hardcodes its own local server (127.0.0.1:PORT) and needs TEXTGEN_PROVIDER=dictionary and a test clock, so `team-play test` found no tests for it. I only confirmed that the deployed garage opens on a phone and that the random generator works there.

I could not play the textgen scenarios. The T-0091 spec starts its own local server with TEXTGEN_PROVIDER=dictionary, and `team-play test` found no tests for it and had no local server to use. The deployed host, which has no flag, shows no description field in the visible garage area, but the page is cut off and the test run was inconclusive. The deployed /healthz version db052a4 differs from the released commit e38635c.

The textgen scenarios could not run: against a deployed host the config runs only @live specs, and the textgen specs are not tagged @live. Only the hidden-field default was seen on the phone screenshot; the other criteria rest on the dispatcher's unit run (149 passed).

I could not run the T-0031 e2e spec: against the deployed host `team-play test` only runs tests tagged @live, and opponent-specs.spec.ts has no such tag, so Playwright reported "No tests found". The live host also reports version 4e47e1e, not the task commit 61d6884, and I only saw the menu screen at 360×740, so no acceptance criterion was verified in a browser.

The textgen specs are correctly absent from the production run, and the clock endpoint answers 404 on the live host. I could not run the 25/day limit or the 60 s block in a browser, because team-play only runs against the deployed host and those specs spawn their own server.

I could not play the T-0031 e2e spec against the deployed host. The runner only runs specs tagged @live there, and opponent-specs.spec.ts has no such tag, so every grep returned "No tests found". No two-context scenario ran, so no acceptance criterion was verified by play.

Against the deployed host, both textgen specs are not selected and the phone garage shows no description field, which is consistent with criterion 4 and the production negative case. The limit, localStorage and 60 s block scenarios need a local server with TEXTGEN_PROVIDER, which I couldn't start, so they were not played.

I could not play the main criterion. The two-context opponent-spec test is untagged for live mode, so Playwright found no tests against the deployed host. The full desktop run passed 14 and failed 3 for environmental reasons, and the deployed version is not shown to contain the task commit.

The deployed host's version (25339d2…) differs from the task commit (3875a33…). Its metrics.json has no balance block, and a Playwright battle would be skipped as test traffic anyway, so the feature could not be observed. Only the smoke spec ran, and it passed.
